keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1873-1884 shape is 62 cells: 40 in Ghana (the coast) and 20 at Lagos, Nigeria. Lagos was a separate colony (declared 5 March 1862, 'The administration was merged with that of Sierra Leone in 1866, and was transferred to the Gold Coast in 1874', separate again in 1886), so it is a dependency (vassal events, dossier lagos-colony), not Gold Coast land. The Dutch forts came on 6 April 1872 and the crown colony was proclaimed on 24 July 1874 (Gold Coast page), so 1873 shows the incorporated coast before the proclamation. Review fix: this outline covers 1873 only; from the Fomena settlement of 1874 the colony reaches inland (british-gold-coast_1874).

region.text: all Danish forts and settlements, including Christiansborg, Fredensborg, Prinsensten, Kongensten and Augustaborg

ledger.note: 1850: the Danish forts join the Gold Coast. Infobox 'Incorporation of the Danish Gold Coast: 1850'; 'the coastal administration was separated from Sierra Leone in 1850'. The Danish Gold Coast page (second page): 'On 30 March 1850 all of Denmark's Danish Gold Coast Territorial Settlements and forts ... were sold' to Britain, 'later incorporated into the British Gold Coast'; the five forts are Christiansborg (Accra), Fredensborg (Old Ningo), Prinsensten (Keta), Kongensten (Ada) and Augustaborg (Teshie). The capital moves to Christiansborg in 1877.

6 April 1872: Britain takes over the Dutch Gold Coast. 'In 1872, British influence over the Gold Coast increased further when Britain purchased the Dutch Gold Coast' (infobox 'Incorporation 6 April 1872').

ledger.note: 1873: the Asante invade the new British protectorate. 'The Ashanti invaded the new British protectorate' after Britain bought the Dutch Gold Coast in 1872; the page dates the Third Anglo-Ashanti War from 1873 and the Gold Coast page speaks of the Asante's 'last invasion of the coast in 1873'. The zone is the Central region round Elmina and Cape Coast, as in the ashanti-empire dossier.

ledger.note: 1874: Lagos is placed under the Gold Coast. 'The administration was merged with that of Sierra Leone in 1866, and was transferred to the Gold Coast in 1874'; in 1877 the Lagos government was 'subordinate to Accra'.

region.text: the coast round Elmina and Cape Coast

ledger.note: 4 February 1874: the British take Kumasi and the war is won. Kumasi 'was abandoned by the Ashanti when the British arrived on 4 February and was briefly occupied by the British'; the Gold Coast page: the January 1874 attack 'resulted in the occupation and burning of Kumasi'. The page dates the Treaty of Fomena to July 1874 (the Fomena page used by ashanti-empire says February).

24 July 1874: the Gold Coast Colony is proclaimed. 'The British, following their defeat of Asante in 1874, proclaimed the former coastal protectorate a crown colony'; the 'Gold Coast Colony, established on 24 July 1874, comprised the coastal areas'. The inland extension that followed the treaty is the gain event of the same month.

'The Gold Coast Colony, established on 24 July 1874, comprised the coastal areas and extended inland as far as the ill-defined borders of Asante'; 'The subsequent peace treaty required the Asante to renounce any claim to many southern territories.' The year and the inland extension are the page's; the region (Central and Eastern, the land the ashanti-empire dossier books as its 1874 loss, without Adanse round Obuasi, which that dossier adds) is the researcher's reading, so confidence 2.
1877: the colonial capital moves from Cape Coast to Accra (Christiansborg). Infobox 'Cape Coast (1821-1877) Accra (1877-1957)'.
1886: Lagos becomes a separate colony again. 'In 1886 Lagos became a separate colony from the Gold Coast under Governor Cornelius Alfred Moloney.'

wars.name: Third Anglo-Ashanti War

zones.text: the coast round Elmina and Cape Coast

wars.outcome: British victory in 1874; the Asante were required 'to renounce any claim to many southern territories' and the Gold Coast Colony was proclaimed on 24 July 1874.
wars.note: Review fix: the zone is the Central region round Elmina and Cape Coast, as in ashanti-empire. The Anglo-Ashanti wars page (opened 2026-10-25) dates the war 1873-1875, the Asante invasion of the new British protectorate in 1873 and the British arrival at Kumasi on 4 February 1874; it gives the Treaty of Fomena as July 1874. The Gold Coast page: 'comprised the coastal areas and extended inland'; the colony proclaimed 24 July 1874.

wars.name: Fourth Anglo-Ashanti War
wars.outcome: Kumasi occupied in January 1896 without fighting; the Asante state became a protectorate (1896 on the Gold Coast page, 1897 on the Anglo-Ashanti wars page).
wars.note: Review fix: 26 December 1895 to 4 February 1896; 'Not a shot had been fired' (Anglo-Ashanti wars page) and 'Ashanti was once again occupied by British troops in January 1896' (War of the Golden Stool page), so no ground was fought over and the zones are empty; the vassal_start of January 1896 carries the change.

wars.outcome: The German colony surrendered on 26 August 1914; British forces occupied the west (British Togoland page: 'Occupation: 27 August 1914').
wars.note: The Gold Coast dossier lists the war because British troops entered from the Gold Coast; the Togoland page says only that 'French and British troops invaded unopposed' on 7 August 1914 (the Gold Coast Regiment is not named on the pages opened). Contest and occupation events are in german-africa and british-togoland.

certainty.note: Forts, a coastal protectorate and (from 1896) the Ashanti and northern treaty areas with no surveyed lines on the pages opened; the Fante and Asante frontiers moved by treaty and conquest.

'In 1898 and 1899, European colonial powers amicably demarcated the boundaries between the Northern Territories and the surrounding French and German colonies' (Gold Coast page). The Anglo-French line in Togoland (27 December 1916) is an administrative line; Lagos in 1874-1886 was a dependency, not a frontier.

notes:
Dossier written by af-08-c from nine pages (Gold Coast, Northern Territories, British Togoland, Lagos Colony, Niger Coast Protectorate, Colony and Protectorate of Nigeria, British Cameroons, War of the Golden Stool, German Togoland).

The Cliopatria row 'British Gold Coast' (1873-1960) is a composite, not the Gold Coast: by the gazetteer, 1873: 40 Ghana + 20 Lagos cells; 1885-1897: 59-75 Ghana + about 527 Nigeria cells; 1900: 1,146 Ghana + 841 Nigeria; 1905 on: Nigeria entire (3,736-3,850 cells) plus Ghana and, from 1916, 201 cells of the British Cameroons; 1960: Nigeria and the Cameroons with no Ghana. This dossier keeps the Ghana part only (every keyframe is 'adjust' except 1960, 'wrong') and treats the Nigerian and Cameroons pieces as belonging to lagos-colony, niger-coast-protectorate, northern-nigeria-protectorate / colony-and-protectorate-of-nigeria (siblings), federal-republic-of-nigeria and a British Cameroons dossier that does not yet exist (counterparts_needing_dossiers: 'British Cameroons', 1916 to 1961; the Cameroons were run as part of Nigeria). The row's end year (1960) is wrong for Ghana: the Gold Coast ends on 6 March 1957 and Cliopatria's Ghana row starts in 1958.

State definition: the pages call the colony 'established: 1821' with the capital at Cape Coast, so the dossier starts 1821 although Cliopatria starts 1873; the pre-1872 extent is a 30 km placeholder (page silent), the Danish forts are booked here as a 1850 gain from danish-gold-coast (that dossier names british-colonial-empire), and the Dutch forts arrive on 6 April 1872 (matching dutch-gold-coast's dissolve). Lagos is shown as a dependency (vassal events 1874-1886, 'transferred to the Gold Coast in 1874'; 'In 1886 Lagos became a separate colony'). Ashanti is a protectorate from January 1896 (vassal tint) and a colony from 26 September 1901 (some pages say 1902; Order in Council date taken from the reference list of the War of the Golden Stool page, not its body). British Togoland is its own state (dossier british-togoland, written here as a direct counterpart that no Cliopatria row covers) administered as part of the Gold Coast from 27 December 1916 to December 1956 (vassal tint).

Disagreements and gaps. The ashanti-empire dossier books a 1874 'loss' of Assin, Akim, Adanse and Denkyira to the British; the Gold Coast page says only that the Asante had to 'renounce any claim to many southern territories' and that the colony 'comprised the coastal areas', so no matching gain is recorded here. The 1899 frontier events (France, Germany) are only 'amicably demarcated' on the page: the treaties and the 1899 Togoland Neutral Zone / Volta Triangle bargain (German Togoland page, outcome not stated) are open. The Northern Territories chiefdoms (Mamprusi, Dagbon, Gonja, Wa) have no dossier of their own in this batch. The Cliopatria 1873-1884 Ghana patch (40 cells) is much smaller than the Dutch and British coast the pages describe; the Cliopatria shapes are kept as drawn for those years. The ghana dossier equates British Togoland with the Volta Region; by Cliopatria's German Togoland shape it is 79 cells, of which 49 lie in Volta and 30 outside, while 52 Volta cells (Keta, Ada) were already Gold Coast Colony in 1900.

No ruler strip (governors were not listed on the pages opened). Page budget 9 of 9: not opened were the Treaty of Fomena and the Third Anglo-Ashanti War page, the Anglo-French and Anglo-German border agreements of 1898-1899, and the Colony of Lagos / Northern Nigeria pages for the Nigerian cells.


Repairs of 2026-10-25 (review af-08-c; 11 pages in all, two over the original budget of 9). (1) 1850 gain of the Danish forts from danish-gold-coast (Gold Coast infobox 'Incorporation of the Danish Gold Coast: 1850'; 30 March 1850 on the Danish Gold Coast page); keyframes split 1821-1849 / 1850-1871 and the 1872 outline unioned with the 1873 coastal strip so that 1872 and 1873 agree. The danish-gold-coast dossier still names british-colonial-empire as counterpart and successor: its group should change both to british-gold-coast. (2) Third Anglo-Ashanti War: mirror contest pair (1873, 4 February 1874) with ashanti-empire on the Central coast, and a 24 July 1874 gain of the Central and Eastern regions at confidence 2 (the page says only that the colony 'extended inland as far as the ill-defined borders of Asante'; ashanti-empire books Central, Eastern and Adanse as its loss and its Fomena page dates the treaty February against July here). New keyframe 1874-1884 and the 1885-1895 outlines unioned with the gain: Cliopatria's Ghana part (40-75 cells) stops at the coast. Not agreed: Adanse (Obuasi) and the Brong, which ashanti-empire books as lost but this page does not give to the colony. (3) War of the Golden Stool: contest_start March and contest_end September 1900 against 'Asante rebels under Yaa Asantewaa'; the Fourth Anglo-Ashanti War has empty zones ('Not a shot had been fired'). (4) The Ashanti vassal pair and the 1901 gain now use Cliopatria's Ashanti 1895 shape less the Central, Eastern and Northern Territories cells, which are direct land in this dossier. (5) The 1897 Northern Territories gain covers Northern, Upper West and Upper East (confidence 2: the page names Bona, Dagarti, Wa and Mamprusi and no regions); the 1899 'nobody' gain keeps only the frontier remainder (13 cells) and the 1898 keyframe is unioned with the Territories. (6) NOT changed, routed to the ashanti-empire group (af-04): the vassal pair and the 1901 gain keep counterpart ashanti-empire although that dossier dissolves in 1896/1 (counterpart british-gold-coast): either the Asante state should run to 26 September 1901 as a protectorate with vassal events of its own, or this dossier would have to book the land as a 1896 gain and lose the protectorate tint; the pages support the protectorate (1896 Gold Coast page, 1897 Anglo-Ashanti page) and the colony of 26 September 1901, so the vassal reading was kept. Still open from the review's gap list: the Bond of 1844 as a vassal candidate (the Gold Coast page gives an 'informal protectorate' with no territory or dated end), the 40 to 75 cell growth of Cliopatria's Ghana part 1873-1890 (the 40 to 59 growth is the Volta-delta coast east of Accra, bbox 0.33 to 1.01 E), and the 1898-1899 frontier treaties.
